findings.title: Plugin request logs no longer include traceID
findings.body: The previous LoggerMiddleware explicitly appended `traceID` from `tracing.TraceIDFromContext` to the log parameters. This change removes that field, and the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware only adds endpoint, plugin ID, data source, and user fields. Unless an earlier middleware independently injects traceID into the contextual logger, plugin request log lines will no longer contain traceID, weakening trace correlation.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards logs and context
findings.body: TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new TestLogger instead of a logger that shares the receiver's recorded log state or carries contextual attributes. Because LoggerMiddleware now logs via `logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, tests injecting TestLogger will not observe emitted log records on the original fake, and contextual fields added by ContextualLoggerMiddleware cannot be verified. The fake should return a child/logger that records into the same state or preserves context.

findings.title: MetricsMiddleware is a shared mutable middleware instance
findings.body: NewMetricsMiddleware creates one *MetricsMiddleware and the returned middleware function mutates `imw.next` each time it is applied, returning the same instance. If the middleware value is used to build more than one client chain, or applied concurrently, the `next` field can be overwritten or raced, causing requests from one chain to be dispatched to another chain's next client. Middleware factories should construct a new wrapper per `next` or avoid mutable shared state.

findings.title: No tests for new contextual logger middleware
findings.body: The PR introduces ContextualLoggerMiddleware and changes LoggerMiddleware to rely on `FromContext`, but the only changed test is a rename of the metrics middleware test. There are no tests verifying that QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, and CollectMetrics contexts are enriched with endpoint/plugin/data source/user attributes, or that stream endpoints are intentionally excluded. Without such tests, future changes can silently drop contextual log fields.
